title: Analogies: Find the Relationship
learning_objectives: Identify the relationship between a pair of words or numbers.
Apply the same relationship to a second pair.
Explain why one option fits better than the alternatives.

sections.heading: What is an analogy?
sections.body: An analogy asks you to recognize a relationship in one pair and apply the same relationship to another pair. Do not match words merely because they are associated; state the exact relationship first.

sections.heading: A four-step method
sections.body: 1. Read the first pair. 2. Say the relationship in a short sentence. 3. Apply that sentence to the second pair. 4. Check every option and eliminate choices that change the relationship.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Bird : nest :: bee : hive. A bird may live in a nest, and a bee colony lives in a hive. The relation is animal-to-dwelling, so 'hive' completes the pair.

sections.heading: Avoid common traps
sections.body: Avoid loose associations. If the first pair describes a tool and its function, the second pair should preserve that same direction and level of specificity. Check whether more than one option could reasonably fit.

questions.explanation: The relationship is an animal and its typical dwelling. A bee colony lives in a hive.
The first item is commonly acted on by the verb: people read a book and eat food.
The first number is squared: 3 × 3 = 9, so 4 × 4 = 16.
A glove is worn on a hand; a sock is worn on a foot. Shoes are also worn on feet, but among these options 'sock' best preserves the clothing-item relation and specificity.
A puppy is a young dog; a kitten is a young cat.

flashcards.front: What is the first step in solving a word analogy?
flashcards.back: State the exact relationship in the first pair in a short sentence.

flashcards.front: What should you check after choosing an analogy answer?
flashcards.back: Verify that the same relationship and direction apply to both pairs.
A pair of numbers connected by a rule, such as squaring or doubling.

flashcards.front: How do you avoid loose associations?
flashcards.back: Prefer the most precise relationship that fits the original pair and test it against every option.
